outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no source I could open settles the Mahler-measure form of Lehmer's conjecture (an absolute constant C > 1 bounding from below the Mahler measure of every non-cyclotomic integer polynomial), and every 2025-2026 source I read still treats it as open. The window holds restricted-class results (a p-adic criterion for conjugates in a p-adic field, 2025; a complete treatment of reciprocal length-5 polynomials, published online January 2025), results that assume the conjecture (McKee and Smyth, May 2026; Mehrabdollahi's talk, May 2026), a 2024 lower bound for Salem numbers alone by an author whose 2017 and 2019 claimed full proofs were criticised in print, and a 2025 French preprint (Amara, revised 30 September 2026) that says it 'disproves Lehmer's conjecture' but, on my reading, concerns a different statement about Salem and Pisot accumulation points.
problem_asks: (1) Wikipedia's January 2024 wording (lead, as opened): whether there is an absolute constant mu > 1 such that every integer polynomial that is not a product of cyclotomic polynomials (times a monomial) has Mahler measure at least mu; equivalently, whether 1 is a limit point from above of Mahler measures of such polynomials. The bullet names it 'Lehmer's conjecture on the Mahler measure of non-cyclotomic polynomials'. Literature variants I treat as the same question: the same claim over non-root-of-unity algebraic integers or algebraic numbers (Lehmer's problem as usually stated). A degree-dependent constant, as in Dobrowolski's bound, is a different and weaker claim. (2) Not asked explicitly by the bullet, but stated in the lead as 'widely believed': the sharp form, that the least Mahler measure above 1 is attained at Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial z^10 + z^9 - z^7 - z^6 - z^5 - z^4 - z^3 + z + 1, with measure about 1.1762808. Recorded so the later pass can see both parts.

events.what_happened: Dobrowolski's lower bound for the Mahler measure of a non-cyclotomic polynomial of degree d, of order (log log d / log d)^3 (Wikipedia, Lehmer's conjecture article, 'Partial results'). Primary paper not opened; the constant 1/1200 appears in a search summary only.
events.delivers: For each degree d, a positive lower bound on the Mahler measure of a non-cyclotomic polynomial of degree d, tending to 1 only like (log log d / log d)^3. The constant depends on the degree.
events.remains: A lower bound that does not depend on the degree. This is the uniform constant that part (1) of problem_asks requires.
events.direction: Partial, in the direction of the conjecture (a bound above 1), but only degree by degree.

events.what_happened: Voutier's explicit version of the degree-dependent bound, with explicit constant C >= 1/4 for degree D >= 2 (Wikipedia, 'Partial results'). Primary paper not opened.
events.delivers: An explicit degree-dependent lower bound for Mahler measures of non-cyclotomic polynomials. The constant is fixed, but the bound still decays with the degree.
events.remains: A lower bound that does not depend on the degree.
events.direction: Partial, in the direction of the conjecture, degree-dependent.

events.what_happened: McKee and Smyth, 'Integer symmetric matrices of small spectral radius and small Mahler measure' (arXiv:0907.0371). They find all minimal noncyclotomic integer symmetric matrices and solve the strong form of Lehmer's problem for this class: every noncyclotomic integer symmetric matrix has Mahler measure at least Lehmer's number 1.17628.
events.revisions: v1 only, 2 Jul 2009.
events.delivers: Lehmer's bound with the sharp constant, but only for integer symmetric matrices (matrix Mahler measure), not for integer polynomials or algebraic numbers.
events.remains: Integer polynomials and algebraic numbers in general, i.e. part (1) and the sharp form in part (2) for polynomials.
events.direction: Proves the sharp form, but only for a restricted class (symmetric integer matrices).

events.what_happened: G. Taylor, 'Lehmer's conjecture for matrices over the ring of integers of some imaginary quadratic fields' (arXiv:1103.4579). Proves that any noncyclotomic matrix over R = O of Q(sqrt(d)) for squarefree d < 0, d not equal to -1 or -3, has Mahler measure at least lambda_0 = 1.176..., and the same for the associated reciprocal polynomials.
events.revisions: v1 only, 23 Mar 2011.
events.delivers: A Lehmer-type bound with the sharp constant, but only for matrices over rings of integers of certain imaginary quadratic fields and for their associated reciprocal polynomials.
events.remains: Integer polynomials and algebraic numbers in general.
events.direction: Proves the sharp form for a restricted class of matrices.

events.what_happened: Choi and Samuels, 'Two inequalities on the areal Mahler measure' (arXiv:1408.5040). They improve two inequalities of Pritsker for the areal Mahler measure, focusing on small values, which the abstract calls 'most relevant to Lehmer's conjecture'.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: Inequalities for the areal Mahler measure, a different quantity from the Mahler measure in the statement. The abstract ties its small-value focus to Lehmer's conjecture; I did not establish any bound on the Mahler measure itself.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Neighbouring. It is about a different quantity, and does not change what the problem asserts.

events.what_happened: Will Y. Lee, 'Elementary Proof of Lehmer's Conjecture on Non-vanishing of Ramanujan's Tau Function' (arXiv:1506.02098). It claims to prove that tau(n) is nonzero for all n >= 1. This is D. H. Lehmer's tau conjecture, a namesake and not the Mahler-measure problem. The author withdrew the paper in version 2.
events.revisions: v1 6 Jun 2015; v2 17 Jun 2016, marked withdrawn.
events.delivers: Claims non-vanishing of Ramanujan's tau function. Not about Mahler measure.
events.remains: Not applicable; the claim concerns a different problem that shares the name.
events.doubts: The arXiv comments field says: 'The proof for Lemma 2 and Lemma 4 turned out to be false.' A search snippet also mentions a computational verification to n <= 22798241520242687999 by Bosman, which I did not open.

withdrawn.what: Author withdrew the paper. The comments field says the proofs of Lemma 2 and Lemma 4 turned out to be false.

events.direction: Claims a proof of a different conjecture that shares D. H. Lehmer's name. Withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Borwein, Dobrowolski and Mossinghoff, 'Lehmer's problem for polynomials with odd coefficients', Annals of Mathematics 166 (2007), 347-366. For a polynomial with no cyclotomic factors and all coefficients odd, the Mahler measure is bounded below by a constant times (1 - 1/n), which the authors describe as resolving Lehmer's problem for this class.
events.delivers: A uniform constant above 1, but only for polynomials whose coefficients are all odd and that have no cyclotomic factors. The constant is stated as (log 5)/4 times (1 - 1/n) on the Annals page I opened; a search summary gives log(5/4)(1 - 1/n). I did not resolve which is correct.
events.remains: Polynomials with some even coefficients.
events.direction: Proves a uniform lower bound for a restricted class (odd coefficients), in the direction of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: El Otmani, Maul, Rhin and Sac-Epee, 'Finding new small degree polynomials with small Mahler measure by genetic algorithms', Rocky Mountain J. Math. 47(8) (2017), 2619-2626. A genetic-type search for monic irreducible non-cyclotomic integer polynomials with Mahler measure below 1.3. It reports two new polynomials, of degrees 46 and 56, missing from Mossinghoff's list.
events.delivers: A computational enumeration of small Mahler measures. It is not a bound, and the abstract does not report any polynomial below Lehmer's number 1.17628. Genetic algorithms are not AI systems in the sense of section 5.4 unless the paper says otherwise, and I read only the abstract.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. Computation to a finite degree does not establish the uniform constant.

checked_by.who: Rocky Mountain Journal of Mathematics (editorial process)

events.direction: Computational. It shows that the earlier enumeration was incomplete from degree 46, not that anything lies below Lehmer's number.
events.object: Two polynomials of degrees 46 and 56 with Mahler measure below 1.3, missing from Mossinghoff's list. Their coefficients and values were not read.

events.what_happened: Jean-Louis Verger-Gaugry, 'A Proof of the Conjecture of Lehmer and of the Conjecture of Schinzel-Zassenhaus' (arXiv:1709.03771; also HAL hal-01584495). A 164-page preprint whose abstract states: 'The conjecture of Lehmer is proved to be true.' The method uses Parry upper functions, dynamical zeta functions of Renyi-Parry systems, lenticular minorants and Poincare asymptotic expansions.
events.revisions: v1 only, 12 Sep 2017 (per arXiv page as read).
events.delivers: Claims the full conjecture: a uniform constant above 1 for all non-cyclotomic polynomials (and, per the title, Schinzel-Zassenhaus). If the claim held, it would settle part (1) of problem_asks. The sharp form in part (2) is not claimed.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim held. The claim is contested (see doubts).

checked_by.qualification: A number theorist working on Mahler measure and heights. A search summary shows his co-authored work on the topic; I did not verify his affiliation in this run.
checked_by.what_they_did: Posted a one-page remark (arXiv:1809.10600, 23 Sep 2018) saying that, as several specialists had remarked, the 2017 proof contains at least one fatal error. The note does not say what the error is, according to the abstract page I opened. A search summary says the note focuses on Theorem 5.23 of the 2017 preprint; I did not verify that against the note's full text.

events.doubts: (a) Amoroso's 2018 remark, as read in its abstract and in a search summary: several specialists found at least one fatal error. The error is not specified in the text I could read, and the 2017 preprint is not known to have been corrected. (b) The 2019 version (next event) reuses the same framework, and an arXiv admin note records substantial text overlap with this preprint. (c) No journal publication, referee report, or published response to Amoroso was found. The 2017 full text was unreadable through my fetch tool, so I could not check the argument itself.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture in its full form, that is, a uniform lower bound above 1 for Mahler measures of non-cyclotomic polynomials. This cuts in the direction the statement's wording points.

events.what_happened: Breuillard and Varju, 'On the Lehmer conjecture and counting in finite fields' (arXiv:1810.13363). The abstract gives a reformulation of the Lehmer conjecture as a counting problem modulo p. It claims no bound and no proof.
events.delivers: Nothing on whether the conjecture holds. It is a reformulation.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Neutral. Recorded as a reformulation, not a result.

events.what_happened: Vesselin Dimitrov, 'A proof of the Schinzel-Zassenhaus conjecture on polynomials' (arXiv:1912.12545). Abstract: for an integer polynomial P of degree n with P(0) = 1, either P is a product of cyclotomic polynomials or at least one complex root lies in |z| <= 2^(-1/(4n)). This is the house problem of Schinzel and Zassenhaus, a neighbouring question and a different quantity.
events.revisions: v1 only, 28 Dec 2019. The Annals of Mathematics listing (annals.math.princeton.edu/articles/22975) appeared in a search result and I did not open it.
events.delivers: A house lower bound for algebraic integers (roots outside a small disc), not a Mahler measure bound. It does not settle Lehmer's conjecture, though the two are related.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Neighbouring. A different conjecture with a related house bound.

events.what_happened: Jean-Louis Verger-Gaugry, 'A proof of the Conjecture of Lehmer' (arXiv:1911.10590). The abstract, as I read it through a summary, says it proves Lehmer's conjecture and the Schinzel-Zassenhaus conjecture, gives a Dobrowolski-type bound, and shows that Salem numbers are bounded below by theta_31^(-1) of about 1.08545. It also says whether Lehmer's number is the smallest Salem number 'remains open'. Uses Parry upper functions and dynamical zeta functions of beta-shifts.
events.revisions: v1 24 Nov 2019; v2 29 Oct 2021. The v2 comments say: 'Results unchanged, revised arguments in Section 5' and 'Theorem 10.1 and its proof were revised'. An arXiv admin note records substantial text overlap with arXiv:1709.03771.
events.delivers: Claims the full conjecture (a uniform constant above 1 for non-cyclotomic polynomials), as in the 2017 preprint. It claims that Lehmer's number is not established as the least Salem number.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim held. The claim is contested (see doubts).
events.doubts: (a) It shares a framework and text with the 2017 preprint, which Amoroso's 2018 remark reports to contain at least one fatal error. (b) The v2 comments say revisions were made to Section 5 and Theorem 10.1, but I could not read the full text: the PDF is unreadable through my fetch tool and the HTML version returns 404, so I could not check whether the objection is answered. (c) No journal publication, referee report, or response to Amoroso was found. A 2022 seminar abstract still cites this paper as an attack on the conjecture, according to a search snippet I did not open.
events.direction: Claims the full conjecture, as above.

events.what_happened: Berend Ringeling, 'On Lehmer's question for integer-valued polynomials' (arXiv:2207.06990, 14 July 2022). The abstract says: 'We solve a Lehmer-type question about the Mahler measure of integer-valued polynomials.' A search summary says the journal version appeared in the Journal de Theorie des Nombres de Bordeaux in 2024 and that the family (x^p - x)/p gives reducible integer-valued polynomials with Mahler measure arbitrarily close to, but above, 1. I did not open the journal version.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only, 14 Jul 2022. Journal version reported in 2024 (search summary, not opened).
events.delivers: A Lehmer-type statement for integer-valued polynomials, a different class from integer polynomials. Per the search summary, the analogue fails there: there is no gap above 1.
events.remains: Problem_asks for integer polynomials and algebraic numbers.
events.directly_checkable: Per the search summary, the family (x^p - x)/p is an explicit family of integer-valued polynomials. I did not verify it.
events.direction: Variant. Cuts against the analogue for integer-valued polynomials, not against the statement for integer polynomials.
events.object: Per the search summary, reducible integer-valued polynomials with Mahler measure arbitrarily close to 1 from above, from the family (x^p - x)/p. Not verified.

events.what_happened: Haydar Goral, 'Lehmer's conjecture via model theory', Proc. Japan Acad. Ser. A 98(7) (2022), 52-55, DOI 10.3792/pjaa.98.010. States a 'Bounded Lehmer's conjecture' and proves it under a hypothesis: if a certain formula is uniformly stable in a class of structures, the bounded version holds. The proof uses van der Waerden's theorem.
events.revisions: Journal online 14 July 2022. No earlier arXiv version found.
events.delivers: A conditional reduction. Under a uniform-stability hypothesis, a bounded version holds: for each B, a constant for a restricted class A_B. My search summary says A_B is defined by a degree-related condition, which I did not confirm.
events.remains: The uniform-stability hypothesis, which I did not find verified for any formula, and the full conjecture.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the Japan Academy, Series A (editorial process)

events.doubts: Conditional, so it establishes no unconditional case. A later talk abstract by the same author describes the conjecture as still open, per a search snippet.
events.direction: Conditional reduction, in the direction of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Mounir Hajli, 'Toward a generalization of Lehmer's problem to adelic curves' (arXiv:2405.15572). It shows that Lehmer's problem generalises to a natural adelic curve, and investigates the problem over finitely generated fields over Q.
events.revisions: v1 24 May 2024; v2 9 Dec 2025, marked 'the final version of the manuscript, accepted for publication' (journal not named).
events.delivers: A generalisation to adelic curves, which is a different setting from the Mahler measure of polynomials. It establishes no bound for integer polynomials.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Analogue. A generalisation of the problem to a different setting.

events.what_happened: Sara Checcoli and Gabriel Andreas Dill, 'New evidence for Remond's generalisation of Lehmer's conjecture' (arXiv:2506.18776, 23 June 2025, 33 pages). The authors extend a result of Pottmeyer from the multiplicative group to almost split semiabelian varieties over number fields, and prove a group-theoretic statement about rational points that bears on Remond's generalisation.
events.revisions: v1 only, 23 Jun 2025.
events.delivers: A result on Remond's generalisation of Lehmer's conjecture for semiabelian varieties, a different setting from Mahler measure of polynomials.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Analogue. Not about the statement as given.

events.what_happened: Anup B. Dixit and Sushant Kala, 'A p-adic criterion for Lehmer's conjecture' (arXiv:2507.20141, 27 July 2025, 10 pages). Gives lower bounds for the logarithmic Weil height of an algebraic number alpha of degree d in terms of how many of its conjugates lie in a finite extension K of Q_p. The consequence stated in the abstract: Lehmer's conjecture holds for all alpha for which about sqrt(d log d) of its conjugates lie in one finite extension of some Q_p. Corollary 1.4 applies to all non-torsion algebraic numbers.
events.revisions: v1 only, 27 Jul 2025.
events.delivers: Lehmer's conjecture (a lower bound on height, hence on Mahler measure, away from 1) for the restricted class of algebraic numbers with many conjugates in a finite extension of one Q_p, with a count of order sqrt(d log d). Corollary 1.4 gives the count as |S_K(alpha)| >= sqrt(q^3 [K:Q_p] d log d). Not a claim about the general case.
events.remains: Algebraic numbers with fewer conjugates in any p-adic extension, which is the general case of part (1).
events.doubts: The arXiv abstract page I read gives the threshold as order sqrt(d log d). The HTML version's abstract wording, as summarised to me, reads d log d. Its Corollary 1.4 gives sqrt(q^3 [K:Q_p] d log d). I did not resolve this discrepancy, and the threshold is a restriction of the class either way.
events.direction: Proves a Lehmer-type bound for a restricted class, in the direction of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Mohamed Amara, 'Nombres de Pisot, nombres de Salem et la conjecture de Lehmer' (arXiv:2509.21402). In French, 31 pages. Abstract, as I read it through a summary: every accumulation point of the Salem set T lies in the Pisot set S, so S union T is closed in (1, +infinity). The author says this settles Boyd's conjecture and disproves Lehmer's conjecture. Introduction: 'D'apres Lehmer [5], la reciproque serait impossible', i.e. Lehmer is cited as holding that Salem numbers cannot accumulate at Pisot numbers. 'Ce resultat permet de rejeter la conjecture de Lehmer.' The key result is Lemma 3.5 (accumulation points of T lie in S).
events.revisions: v1 24 Sep 2025; v2 30 Sep 2026. The arXiv page shows no change note for v2.
events.delivers: Per the paper's own statements, a closedness result for S union T in (1, +infinity), together with a claimed smallest element tau_0. The introduction, as I read it, calls tau_0 the smallest element of S union T; section 2.3.4 calls it 'le plus petit element connu des nombres de Salem'. By my expansion, tau_0 is the zero of 1+z-z^3(1+z+z^2+z^3+z^4)+z^9+z^10, which is Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial. The 'disproof' is of Lehmer's cited claim about accumulation points, not of the Mahler-measure statement. Nothing I read bears on part (1) of problem_asks.
events.remains: All of part (1) of problem_asks. Part (2) (least Salem number) is affected only if the 'smallest element' reading is meant as a theorem; the text I could read leaves that ambiguous.
events.doubts: (a) Preprint only, in French. No journal, specialist response, or review found in my searches. (b) My reading of the introduction, Lemma 3.5 and section 2.3.4 comes from a summary of the HTML text, not from my own reading of the French. (c) The summary says some steps are described as 'heuristic' ('procede heuristique') and that the argument is analytic (Rouche, Schwarz, Montel). No numerical verification appears. (d) The paper's title and the word 'Lehmer' refer to Lehmer's Salem-accumulation claim, not to the Mahler-measure statement, which is a reason a reader could conflate the two.
events.direction: Against Lehmer's cited claim about Salem-Pisot accumulation. Neutral on the Mahler-measure statement.
events.object: Not a counterexample to any Mahler-measure claim. The paper exhibits Pisot numbers as accumulation points of Salem numbers via sequences (gamma_s) and (alpha_s) (Theorem 2.5, per summary), and the smallest element tau_0 of S union T, which is Lehmer's number by my expansion.
people: Mohamed Amara (emeritus professor, Universite de Tunis, per a search summary)

events.what_happened: Jean-Marc Sac-Epee, 'Salem numbers less than 49/37' (arXiv:2409.11159). The abstract says it provides a list of all Salem numbers below 49/37 (about 1.3243). It does not mention Lehmer's problem. A search result shows an earlier HTML version under the title 'Salem numbers less than the plastic constant' (not opened).
events.revisions: v1 17 Sep 2024; v2 16 Jan 2025; v3 31 Jan 2025 (current).
events.delivers: A finite list of Salem numbers below a threshold. It covers only Salem numbers and lists instances. Lehmer's number (about 1.17628) lies below the threshold, but I did not read whether the list establishes that Lehmer's number is the least Salem number.
events.remains: All of part (1) and the sharp form in part (2).
events.directly_checkable: The list itself, which I did not read.
events.direction: Census of instances within a restricted class (Salem numbers below a bound). It does not move a quantity the statement names, and does not establish a uniform constant.
events.object: A list of Salem numbers below 49/37. Contents not read.

events.what_happened: Jean-Louis Verger-Gaugry, 'A Non-Trivial Minoration for the Set of Salem Numbers' (arXiv:2401.05843, v1 11 Jan 2024; written for NUMERATION2023 and dedicated to Christiane Frougny). Theorem 1.1: every Salem number beta exceeds theta_31^(-1) = 1.08544... (theta_n is the root in (0,1) of -1 + x + x^n). Conjecture 1: there is no Salem number in (theta_31^(-1), theta_12^(-1)) = (1.08544..., 1.17295...). Lehmer's number lies in (theta_12^(-1), theta_11^(-1)). The proof uses the dynamical zeta function of the Renyi-Parry system, the Kala-Vavra theorem and Selmer's factorisation of trinomials (per the HTML summary).
events.revisions: v1 only, 11 Jan 2024 (arXiv listing). An arXiv admin note records text overlap with arXiv:1911.10590.
events.delivers: A uniform lower bound of 1.08544... for Salem numbers only. If the proof is correct, this is a Lehmer-type constant for that restricted class. It says nothing about Mahler measures that are not Salem numbers. The conjecture about the gap (1.08544, 1.17295) is not proved.
events.remains: Non-Salem Mahler measures (all of part (1) for them), and the Salem gap conjecture and sharp minimum in part (2).
events.doubts: (a) Same author and framework as the 2017 and 2019 claimed proofs, which Amoroso's 2018 remark reports to contain at least one fatal error. (b) The admin note records substantial text overlap with arXiv:1911.10590. (c) No journal publication or review found. (d) I read the first 100,000 characters of about 128,000 in the HTML version.
events.direction: Restricted to Salem numbers, a uniform lower bound above 1, which cuts in the direction of the conjecture for that class.

events.what_happened: Mahya Mehrabdollahi (Gottingen / MPIM Bonn), talk 'Mahler Measure and Numerical Semigroups', MPIM Bonn, 5 May 2026. The abstract says: 'Using classical results and assuming Lehmer's conjecture, we then provide a proof of a conjecture due to P. Moree and A. Herrera-Poyatos.' No preprint was found.
events.revisions: No write-up located. The talk is dated 5 May 2026; under the date rule, the event would be dated to the write-up, which I could not find.
events.delivers: A conditional result: it proves a Moree and Herrera-Poyatos conjecture assuming Lehmer's conjecture. It establishes no unconditional case.
events.remains: The conjecture itself, which the talk assumes.
events.time_since_posted: about 5 months since the talk; no write-up located
events.doubts: Conditional. Only the abstract page was read.
events.direction: Conditional, so it assumes the conjecture rather than cutting either way.

events.what_happened: James McKee and Chris Smyth, 'Short Salem polynomials' (arXiv:2605.19013, 18 May 2026). The abstract says: 'We give a complete classification of all Salem polynomials of length 5', and 'subject to Lehmer's Conjecture we give a complete list of the 126 exceptions.' Section 1.2 takes Lehmer's conjecture to be the strong form, that lambda_0 (about 1.1762808) is the smallest Salem number. Theorem 2 describes the 126 exceptions as sporadic length-6 Salem polynomials with Salem number at least 1.01: 116 below theta_0 and 10 above.
events.revisions: v1 only, 18 May 2026.
events.delivers: Unconditionally (per the abstract): a classification of length-5 Salem polynomials. Conditionally on the strong form of Lehmer's conjecture for Salem numbers: a complete list of 126 exceptions. The abstract's 'length 5' and Theorem 2's 'length 6' do not match, and I have not resolved which the list refers to.
events.remains: Lehmer's conjecture, which the list assumes, and all of part (1) for non-Salem measures.
events.directly_checkable: The length-5 classification and the 126-element list, which I did not read element by element.
events.doubts: The length mismatch between the abstract and Theorem 2. The conditional list depends on the unproven strong form.
events.direction: Conditional on the conjecture, and an unconditional classification of length-5 Salem polynomials. It does not settle the conjecture.
events.object: A list of 126 exceptional Salem polynomials, conditional on the strong form. Individual entries not read.

events.what_happened: IO+ news article, 9 Oct 2026. It reports that Tom Verhoeff (retired, TU/e) used AI to solve the general case of D. H. Lehmer's 1965 permutation conjecture, which Verhoeff calls 'Lehmer's permutation conjecture'. The article says the binary case was solved earlier and that a preprint is on arXiv. I did not find the preprint. The article names: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), which Verhoeff asked 'to start completely afresh'; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, which 'translated the proof's steps into a program'; Harmonic's Aristotle, which 'wrote the formal verification in Lean'; and, in comparison, GPT-5.2 (OpenAI) and Claude Opus 4.7 (Anthropic).
events.revisions: The binary case is reported as solved in 2016 (Designs, Codes and Cryptography, per a search snippet) or 2017 (per the article). The general case has no preprint I could locate.
events.delivers: Claims the general case of a different conjecture that shares D. H. Lehmer's name: a cycle through permutations of a symbol sequence. Not about Mahler measure.
events.remains: Not applicable to this problem.
events.doubts: Single news source. The authors' own account of the AI's role was not found, so no system is entered under ai.systems.
events.direction: Namesake. Says nothing about the Mahler-measure statement.

events.what_happened: Huimin Zheng, 'Mahler measures at interior CM points: proofs of two conjectures of Samart' (arXiv:2608.02255). Neighbouring Mahler-measure work on identities at CM points. The abstract page does not mention Lehmer's problem or any AI. The HTML version contains a 'Declaration on the use of AI tools' section, quoted via a summary as: 'was carried out by the author with the assistance of the AI system Kimi (Moonshot AI)'. Per the same summary, the declaration credits the AI with computational exploration, the discovery of the proof strategy, machine-certified verifications, and help in preparing the manuscript. The author says they checked and verified all mathematical content.
events.revisions: v1 3 Aug 2026 (abstract page). Later versions not checked.
events.delivers: Proofs of two conjectures of Samart on Mahler measure identities at interior CM points. Not about Lehmer's problem.
events.remains: Not applicable to this problem.

machine_checked.system: Certification scripts described by the author (named in the declaration, per summary)

events.doubts: The AI quotation comes from a summary of the HTML, and I did not check its exact wording against the text. Remaining text (about 41,000 characters of 141,000) was not read.
events.direction: Neighbouring. Settles neighbouring identities, not the Mahler-measure statement.

events.what_happened: Quanyu Tang and Shu Zhang, 'Integral Representations and Asymptotics for a Family of Areal Mahler Measures' (arXiv:2608.01951). Concerns the areal Mahler measure of the family P_m posed by Matilde Lalin. The paper mentions Lehmer only in background. Its 'Statement on AI usage' section, quoted via a summary of the HTML, says: 'ChatGPT proposed the main ideas underlying Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 and assisted in developing their detailed proofs.' It also says the verification programs and certificates for Theorem 1.3 were 'generated with the assistance of ChatGPT', and that 'The human authors subsequently checked, revised, and verified all AI-assisted mathematical arguments'.
events.delivers: Asymptotic and integral representation results for areal Mahler measures of the family P_m. Not about Lehmer's problem.

disputes.summary: Verger-Gaugry's claimed full proofs (arXiv:1709.03771, Sept 2017; arXiv:1911.10590, Nov 2019, revised Oct 2021) are reported by Amoroso's 2018 remark (arXiv:1809.10600) to contain at least one fatal error, as several specialists remarked. No published response, correction, withdrawal or acceptance was found. The 2019 full text was unreadable through my fetch tool, so I could not check whether it answers the objection.

Amara's 2025 preprint says it 'disproves Lehmer's conjecture'. On my reading of its introduction, the statement it rejects is Lehmer's cited claim that Salem numbers cannot accumulate at Pisot numbers, not the Mahler-measure statement. The title also uses 'la conjecture de Lehmer'. This reading rests on a summary of the French text.

The Amara paper identifies its smallest element tau_0 of S union T with Lehmer's number, by my expansion of the polynomial. If the 'smallest element' reading is a theorem, it would address the Salem form of the least-value question in part (2), not only the accumulation claim. The paper also calls tau_0 'the smallest known Salem number'. The text I could read does not settle which is meant.

McKee and Smyth (arXiv:2605.19013): the abstract says a classification of length-5 Salem polynomials and a conditional list of 126 exceptions, while Theorem 2 describes the 126 as length-6 Salem polynomials.

The Verhoeff news report credits Claude Opus 5.5, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Harmonic's Aristotle, GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.7 with roles in a different problem's proof. No authors' account was found, so none is entered under ai.systems. The binary-case year differs between the article (2017) and a search snippet (2016).

summary: I searched for 38 queries covering the name and its variants, the wording a result would use, recent work in the area, and AI involvement, and opened every source I cite where the tool returned the page. The sources are arXiv abstracts and HTML versions, the Wikipedia article (current version, not the January 2024 revision), the Annals, Canadian Mathematical Bulletin and Proceedings of the Japan Academy pages, and Rocky Mountain Journal and MPIM Bonn listings. Nothing in the window settles the Mahler-measure statement or sharpens Lehmer's number, and no source I read reports a counterexample. The events that bear most on the question are as follows. Verger-Gaugry's 2017 and 2019 preprints claim the full conjecture. Amoroso's 2018 remark says several specialists found a fatal error in the 2017 version, and I found no answer to it. The 2019 full text was unreadable, so I could not check whether it responds. Dixit and Kala (July 2025) prove a Lehmer-type bound for algebraic numbers with many conjugates in a p-adic field, a restricted class. El-Serafy and McKee (CMB, online January 2025) treat length-5 reciprocal polynomials in full and length-6 partially, also a restricted class. Verger-Gaugry's January 2024 preprint proves a uniform bound of 1.08544 for Salem numbers only, by the author of the disputed proofs. McKee and Smyth (May 2026) and Mehrabdollahi (May 2026) assume the conjecture, so they are conditional. Amara's September 2025 preprint says it disproves Lehmer's conjecture, but on my reading it concerns Lehmer's cited claim about Salem numbers accumulating at Pisot numbers, not the Mahler-measure statement. It is a same-name case, and it is also the one that could be read as touching part (2), since it identifies the smallest element of S union T with Lehmer's number; the text I could read does not settle that. Two of the close calls are these. The Salem-only bounds (Verger-Gaugry 2024, Dixit-Kala's class, El-Serafy-McKee's length-5 class) are restricted cases, and it is a judgement whether they count toward the problem as stated. Equally, Amara's smallest-element reading would address the sharp form in part (2) only if it is a theorem and not a remark. On AI involvement, I found no AI involvement in any source about the Mahler-measure statement or its Salem sub-problems. I searched for AlphaEvolve, FunSearch, GPT-5, Claude, Erdos-problem AI results, Lean/mathlib formalisation and Aristotle, and found none touching this problem. The AI-involved papers I found are all neighbours. Two Zheng papers (Samart's CM-point identities) name Kimi (Moonshot AI) with a declaration of assistance, and Tang and Zhang (areal Mahler measures of Lalin's family) name ChatGPT, with the authors saying it proposed the main ideas of two theorems. The Verhoeff report names several models for a namesake problem, but I found no authors' account, so it is not entered under systems. Several quotes came through a summariser and are marked as such; they should be checked against the text before anyone relies on their wording.
competing_reading: Read Verger-Gaugry's 2017 and 2019 preprints as correct proofs of the full conjecture, with Amoroso's objection answered in the revision; the 2019 v2 comments say Section 5 and Theorem 10.1 were revised. Or read Amara's paper as a genuine closedness theorem whose smallest element is Lehmer's number, which would give the Salem form of the sharp minimum and would be a second Lehmer-named claim. Or read the 2024 Verger-Gaugry Salem bound and the 2025 Dixit-Kala and El-Serafy-McKee results as genuine partial resolutions of the Mahler question for their classes, since the statement as written asks for a constant and a class-restricted constant is still a constant. The reading I would resist is the one that counts the 2026 conditional papers as progress on the unconditional question.
what_would_settle_it: For Verger-Gaugry: a full readable text of arXiv:1911.10590, or a referee or journal response to Amoroso's objection. For Amara: specialist review of Lemma 3.5 and of the status of tau_0 as the least element of S union T, read from the French §1 and Theorem statements. For McKee and Smyth: the length (5 or 6) of the 126 exceptions. For Verhoeff: the arXiv preprint and its AI declaration. For the uniform constant itself: a proof for all non-cyclotomic polynomials, or a polynomial with Mahler measure in (1, 1.17628), neither of which I found.

dead_ends: No event found for a machine-checked (Lean/Coq) formalisation of Lehmer's polynomial or of any claimed resolution. Searches for mathlib and Lean formalisation returned only the mathematics.

No AI system (AlphaEvolve, FunSearch, GPT-5/OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Aristotle) named in any source about the Mahler-measure statement. The FunSearch paper found (arXiv 2503.11061) benchmarks cap-set, narrow admissible tuples and no-isosceles triangles; it does not treat Salem numbers.
The 2026 arXiv paper 2601.11486 (Newman polynomials, degree-10 measure 1.4194) is not about Lehmer's problem; seen in a search snippet only.
arXiv 2508.08003 (counting Salem numbers from hyperbolic orbifolds, 2025) gives background and was seen only in a snippet; it claims no bound.

Lind (2003, math/0303279; Lehmer constant for compact abelian groups), Lehmer's problem for arbitrary groups (arXiv 1901.00827), Greaves & Taylor (arXiv 1206.1734, Hermitian matrices over Eisenstein and Gaussian integers), and van Ittersum-Ringeling-Zudilin 'Hedgehogs in Lehmer's problem' (2021): analogues or restricted classes, seen only in search snippets and not opened.

incomplete: (1) Verger-Gaugry 2017 (arXiv:1709.03771, 164 pp.) and 2019 (arXiv:1911.10590) full texts could not be read: the PDF tool returned compressed binary and the 2019 HTML returned 404. The Amoroso objection, the 2019 revisions in Section 5 and Theorem 10.1, and whether the 2019 version answers Theorem 5.23 are therefore unchecked. (2) Amara (arXiv:2509.21402): the HTML v2 was read in two portions (about 100,000 and the remainder), so the full text was covered; the PDF was unreadable. My reading of the introduction, Lemma 3.5 and section 2.3.4 comes from summaries of the French text and should be checked against the original. The English abstract was not quoted verbatim, because the fetch summaries cut it at 125 characters. (3) Mehrabdollahi: no preprint found; only the talk listing was read. (4) El-Serafy and McKee: the Cambridge page was read in its first 100,000 of about 117,500 characters, so acknowledgements in the final portion are unchecked (ai.none_found is null for that reason). Its earlier arXiv preprint, if any, was not found, so the date is given at year precision. (5) Verger-Gaugry 2024 (arXiv:2401.05843): the HTML was read in its first 100,000 of about 128,000 characters; ai.none_found is null for that reason. (6) Zheng (arXiv:2609.26120): the first 100,000 of about 187,000 characters were read; the AI declaration was found within that portion, but Lehmer's problem could still be mentioned in the rest. The date conflict (identifier 2609 vs displayed 06 Aug 2026) is unresolved. (7) Zheng (arXiv:2608.02255) and Tang-Zhang (arXiv:2608.01951): the first 100,000 characters of Zheng were read, and the remainder of Tang-Zhang was read in a second portion. The quotations attributed to Kimi and ChatGPT come from summaries of the HTML pages and were not checked against the text. (8) Verhoeff: no arXiv preprint was found; the only source is the IO+ article, which I cite as news. The AI roles are unverified and none is entered under systems. (9) Goral 2022, Ringeling 2022 (journal version), Dobrowolski 1979, Voutier 1996, Smyth 1971 and Borwein-Dobrowolski-Mossinghoff 2007 were dated and characterised from the Wikipedia article, search summaries or journal pages; their primary papers were not read, except BDM's Annals page. (10) The BDM constant is stated differently by two sources ((log 5)/4 times (1-1/n) on the Annals page, and log(5/4)(1-1/n) in a search summary); not resolved. (11) The Wikipedia article read is the current version, not the January 2024 frozen revision, and its lead was paraphrased by a summariser. (12) Journal status was not checked for 2025-2026 preprints (Amara, Dixit-Kala, Checcoli-Dill, Hajli v2 'accepted', McKee-Smyth 2026, Zheng 2026, Tang-Zhang 2026). (13) Mossinghoff's database and zbMATH/MathSciNet/MathOverflow were not checked directly. (14) The AI search (AlphaEvolve, FunSearch, GPT-5, Claude, Gemini, Aristotle, Lean, Erdos-problem AI results, and general AI-assisted Mahler-measure work) found no AI involvement in the Mahler-measure statement or its Salem sub-problems in any source I could read in full. The null values in ai.none_found mean that the full text was not read, not that no system was involved.
